function: GAT-based learned multi-user beamforming at UAV aerial base stations under jamming, jointly with MADDPG-learned UAV deployment and jamming power (pp. 1, 5-8).
system: Air-ground downlink: 4 UAV base stations with 8 antennas each, 4 single-antenna users, 2 single-antenna jammers, 100 m altitude; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 3, 9-10).
method: Hierarchical: inner 3-layer GAT with attention, trained unsupervised on a rate loss; outer MADDPG multi-agent reinforcement learning for UAV deployment and jamming; fine-tuning for new configurations (pp. 6-11).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rician links, large-scale attenuation 30+22log(d) dB, Rician coefficient 10 dB; 50,000 training samples with varied UAV deployments and jamming strategies (p. 10).
test_conditions: GAT trained at the default setting (4 pairs, 2 jammers, 1 W), fine-tuned for 1-11 users, 1-4 jammers, -10 to 40 dBm transmit power (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Beamforming: SCA optimization, MLP, GCN without attention; deployment: multi-agent DDQN and genetic algorithm using the GAT for fitness; initial deployment (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Sum transmission rate (bps/Hz), convergence curves, runtime of 2,000 inferences versus number of users (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Big-O analysis: GAT inference O(D K^2 F^2), training and outer-layer complexity, MLP O(L_M Q^2), SCA O(L_S (KN)^3.5); measured runtime of 2,000 inferences vs users (pp. 9, 12).
q1_support: p. 10: "The wireless links are of Rician model, where the large-scale attenuation follows model of 30+22log(d) in dB"; custom simulator, and no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing set or measured data is named anywhere in the paper.
q2_support: p. 11: "we train the neural network at the default simulation settings, and generalize the inference to new communication scenarios with efficient fine-tune"; p. 12, Fig. 8 caption: "GAT is trained at default setting and generalized to other network configurations with fine tune".
q3_support: p. 10: "we consider the baselines of successive convex approximation (SCA)-based approach, and the general MLP-based learning"; p. 11: "the proposed GAT-based method outperforms all the baselines" (rate, Fig. 8). GCN without attention is an ablation and is not counted.
q4_support: p. 9: "The complexity of the proposed hierarchical learning approach is analyzed as follows" (GAT inference O(D K^2 F^2)); p. 12: "we collectively consider the 2 000 times inference from the trained neural networks" (Fig. 9 runtime).
q5_support: p. 10: "by using 50 000 training samples" produced with the authors' own Rician simulation; the 14 pages contain no code or data link or availability statement, and no public dataset is used.
notes: Title and DOI on page 1 match. The paper is framed as anti-jamming, which is an excluded function, but the learned GAT performs multi-user beamforming of UAV aerial base stations (pp. 5-6), which is beam control for aerial links, and it is learned jointly with UAV deployment, an above-physical decision, so above_phy and function are passed and area 6 wins over 3 as the more specific; if the reviewer reads the function as anti-jamming, the alternative is exclude with reason function. The training paradigm is stated as unsupervised on p. 7 (loss is the negative sum rate, Eq. 21) but as supervised on p. 9. Perfect CSI is assumed (p. 9).
